confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on three web searches run on 2026-11-19. Restaurant, coffee and beer prices come from crowd-sourced cost-of-living aggregates (Numbeo, Expatistan, Wise) plus 2026 travel cost guides. Numbeo lists a cappuccino at about EUR 2.48, a pint of draft beer at EUR 4.25, an inexpensive meal at EUR 15 and a mid-range meal for two at about EUR 66. Cocktail and wine prices come from 2026 guide ranges (cocktails about EUR 10-15, house or local wine about EUR 4-8 a glass) and an Expatistan cocktail figure of EUR 11 that was last updated in March 2025. I converted euros at roughly 1.10 USD per EUR, implied by the RBA AUD rates, and nudged the anchors up slightly for July peak season and prices near the Riva and old town. The RBA observation is taken from a search-result summary that cites rba.gov.au, not from reading the RBA page directly. The accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge. I did not search for them or check live listings. They assume July high-season demand, which is strong in Split, so they are the least certain anchors and could be off by 25-30%.
comparable_city_reasoning: Split is a heavily touristed Adriatic coastal city that uses the euro. Its summer prices are similar to Dubrovnik's (Dubrovnik is somewhat higher) and to other Mediterranean resort cities such as Kotor or the Greek island towns. The accommodation estimates use peak-season patterns from Dalmatian coastal cities.
